question: In June 2026, there was an article entitled ‘From Silence to Strategy: Rethinking Menopause as a European Priority’ in the Media Partner section of ‘The Parliament’ magazine1.

In this article, the Members of the European Parliament Maria Walsh (EPP), Veronika Cifrová Ostrihoňová (Renew), Billy Kelleher (Renew) and Christophe Clergeau (S&D), among others, argued that menopause should to a greater extent be seen as a European health, economic and societal challenge. The article was supported by the pharmaceutical company Besins Healthcare (transparency register number: 7859633100766-19).

The company describes menopause as a policy area where significant health and economic potential could be unlocked through prevention, awareness raising, improved access to treatment and early intervention. Besins Healthcare is an international pharmaceutical group that specialises in hormonal therapies and claims to be the world leader in this field. 1.

Has the Commission assessed the financial impact of extending or increasing public reimbursement for hormone replacement therapies and other menopause treatments, including the resulting market opportunities for pharmaceutical companies?

How does the Commission ensure that menopause policy initiatives are not influenced by the economic interests of companies which market such treatments and at the same time support campaigns, events or media contributions on the issue?

Has the Commission analysed whether and to what extent industry-supported communication and lobbying activities on the issue of menopause have influenced policy priorities at EU level, in particular in the context of the FEMM report 2025/2074(INI)?
Walsh, Maria, et al. „Time for a European Menopause Strategy?“ The Parliament: Total Politics, Juni 2026, S. 15. Special section Women's Health and Menopause, in partnership with Besins Healthcare. 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.10.2026) The World Health Organization (WHO) highlights menopause’s crucial role for women’s healthy ageing and acknowledges its importance as a public health challenge and women’s right imperative1.

The EU Gender Equality Strategy 2026-20302 (GES) recognises that women’s health experiences and conditions, such as menstruation, menopause, endometriosis, and postpartum depression have not received sufficient attention in health research, diagnostics and treatment3.

The Commission has planned to launch in 2028 a study on the macro- and microeconomic and societal benefits of closing the women’s health gap related to certain conditions, like menopause, and will organise an exchange of best practices on measures to effectively combat menstrual and menopause poverty at national level. 1.
At this stage there is no EU Strategy on menopause, and any measures to be taken fall under Member States remit. 2.

In EU pharmaceutical policy, women’s health is not driven or influenced by individual economic considerations but is based on an informed consideration of factors such as the representation of women in clinical research, persistent gaps in understanding sex-based differences in disease and treatment effects, and the need to better integrate these in the development and use of medicines. 3.

The importance of addressing women’s health has always been a priority for the Commission. Menopause is still not routinely integrated into primary healthcare and often remains socially stigmatised, which is why the Commission’s GES draws attention to this issue. The Commission has not analysed to what extent industry-supported communication and lobbying activities have influenced policy priorities at EU level.

1 https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/menopause. 2 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A52026DC0113&qid=1776075756540. 3 See, for example: European Parliament 2025 Report on Gender Inequalities in Medical Research, Drug
